ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 2 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Jim Bridger

code.originalText: Two-week review on the day of the ophthalmology consultation: the eye examination and the surgical plan, the lumbar X-ray, the thyroid ultrasound and back exercise

text.paragraph: Two-week review on the day of the ophthalmology consultation. [S]

Mr. Bridger returns two weeks after intake and was seen this morning by Dr. Delacroix-Moreno of ophthalmology, who dilated his eyes, measured the pressures, scanned both maculas and measured the eyes for lens implants. She found cataracts in both eyes, dense on the right, and no glaucoma, macular degeneration or diabetic eye disease. He has agreed to surgery on the right eye first. He has not driven since intake and has had no new falls; the porch light has been changed for a brighter one. His back aches as before, about 6 out of 10, stiff in the morning and after sitting in the truck; he starts physical therapy on Friday. The lumbar X-ray from intake showed wear in the lower spine and no metal or other foreign body. His thyroid ultrasound this morning showed a multinodular goiter. He has used the diclofenac gel on his knees twice a day without skin trouble. He asked for the plan to be told to him rather than written down, and repeated it back correctly. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 2026-04-21; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Pupils dilated from this morning's examination
Firm multinodular goiter, larger on the left, moving with swallowing; trachea midline; no nodes
Old puckered scar about 2 cm long over the right lower back; tenderness over the lower lumbar facets and the right paraspinal muscles; forward bending to mid-shin, limited by stiffness
Straight-leg raise negative on both sides; strength, reflexes and sensation normal in the legs

Gradual, painless blurring of vision in both eyes over about two years, worse in the right, with glare from sunlight and oncoming headlights, faded colors, and trouble recognizing faces across a room; Snellen acuity 20/200 right and 20/100 left with his old glasses, no better with a pinhole; no flashes, floaters, pain or redness; cause under evaluation with an ophthalmology consultation
S — Synthetic presenting problem anchored to his documented failing eyesight; superseded when the consultation found bilateral cataract.

Bilateral age-related nuclear cataract, dense and brunescent in the right eye and moderate in the left, with cortical spokes; the cause of his reduced vision, glare and color loss; no glaucoma, macular degeneration or diabetic retinopathy; treated with sequential cataract surgery
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis made at the consultation, linked to his documented loss of sight; not a retrospective diagnosis of his real blindness, whose cause is not recorded.

Chronic low back pain for many years, aching across the lower back and worst on the side of an old arrow-wound scar over the right lower back, stiff in the morning and after long rides in his truck; no leg pain, numbness, weakness, bladder or bowel change, fever or weight loss; no red flags
S — Synthetic chronic back pain anchored to his documented arrow wound; which side of the back the arrowhead lay in is not recorded, and the right side is a synthetic choice.
Nontoxic multinodular goiter, present for decades: a firm, nodular, non-tender thyroid enlargement with no pressure symptoms (no trouble swallowing or breathing, no voice change); euthyroid
S — Synthetic modern classification of his documented goiter; the type of his real goiter is not recorded.
Primary osteoarthritis of both knees, aching on stairs and after walking the orchard, with morning stiffness under half an hour, crepitus and bony enlargement
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis anchored to his documented rheumatism; the old term does not name a modern diagnosis.
One fall in the past year, missing the bottom step of the porch at dusk, without injury; poor vision in low light and contrast; at risk of further falls
S — Synthetic fall linked to the reduced vision.

list.item:
Bilateral age-related cataract (H25.13). Dr. Delacroix-Moreno confirms age-related nuclear cataract in both eyes, dense and brunescent on the right, as the cause of the blurred vision, glare and faded colors. Normal pressures and discs exclude glaucoma, and the normal macular OCT and fundus exclude macular degeneration; with an HbA1c of 5.5% there is no diabetic retinopathy. The cataracts stop him recognizing faces, seeing steps at dusk and driving, so surgery is indicated by his loss of function, not by an acuity number. [S]
Right eye phacoemulsification with a monofocal distance lens implant in two weeks; the left eye about six weeks later.
Postoperative drops shown to him with distinct caps and recorded as voice reminders.
No driving until the vision standard is met.

Chronic low back pain (M54.59). Mechanical chronic low back pain from lumbar spondylosis and facet arthropathy, with tenderness near the old arrow-wound scar; no red flags and no nerve root signs. The X-ray shows no retained fragment, so the arrowhead was removed whole and MRI would be safe if it were ever needed; no further imaging is needed now. [S]
Physical therapy from this week: exercise and motor control training, then a home program.
Heat in the morning and staying active; no opioids or muscle relaxants.

Multinodular goiter (E04.2). Euthyroid, with TSH 1.62 and free T4 1.2 at intake. The largest nodule, 1.6 cm, is spongiform, a very low suspicion pattern that would need biopsy only at 2 cm or larger; the others are under 1 cm. No pressure symptoms. [S]
No biopsy now; repeat ultrasound in 18 to 24 months.
Return for trouble swallowing or breathing, voice change or rapid growth.

The VF-14 questionnaire was not given today because he cannot read it and it was not read aloud to him; the surgeon documented his limits by interview (faces across a room, steps at dusk, night driving, glare). No harm: the indication was clear. Corrective action: the VF-14 will be read aloud to him before the second eye's surgery, and the clinic will read questionnaires aloud for patients who do not read

text.paragraph: Guideline basis: Cataract in the Adult Eye Preferred Practice Pattern (2021); Noninvasive Treatments for Acute, Subacute, and Chronic Low Back Pain: A Clinical Practice Guideline From the American College of Physicians (2017); 2015 American Thyroid Association Management Guidelines for Adult Patients with Thyroid Nodules and Differentiated Thyroid Cancer (2015); 2019 American College of Rheumatology/Arthritis Foundation Guideline for the Management of Osteoarthritis of the Hand, Hip, and Knee (2019); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, cataract and rheumatoid arthritis/osteoarthritis monographs (2026); Falls Prevention in Community-Dwelling Older Adults: Interventions (2024)

Follow-up: Right eye surgery in two weeks, with the surgeon's checks at one day and one week. Six-week review here four weeks after the operation. Physical therapy from this week. Next scheduled visit 2026-06-02: six-week review four weeks after right cataract surgery: vision, the drops, falls between operations, back pain and the wrist. [S]
